beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Surya, and this video is about what actually moves between Canvas and our hub, which turns out to be far less than the word integration suggests.

show.event: title snaps in over ground, signal rule above

beats.narration_text: It is easy to assume that integrating two systems means synchronising them. Two things connected, therefore kept in step. Rosters flowing one way, grades flowing back the other. That is not what we built, and the difference is a decision, not an omission.

show.event: two-headed arrow between CANVAS and THE HUB, then struck through in signal

beats.narration_text: Exactly one thing crosses from Canvas to us, and only when a student clicks. The launch token. It carries who they are, which course they are in, what role they hold, and what they clicked. Nothing arrives on a schedule. Nothing is fetched in the background. If nobody clicks, nothing moves.

show.event: single left-to-right arrow carrying LAUNCH TOKEN, three mono lines beneath

beats.narration_text: The links are built out of that, as it happens. The first time a person launches, we record the correspondence between their Canvas identifier and ours. Same for the course. So the database fills up as people arrive. It is never a copy of Canvas made in advance.

show.event: three identifier-pair rows appear one at a time under lti_user_links

beats.narration_text: LTI does have services for real synchronisation. Names and Role Provisioning reads the class roster. Assignment and Grade Services writes to the gradebook. Both are permissions you request when you register the tool. We request neither. Not disabled somewhere in the code, never asked for. The tool cannot read a class list or write a grade, because it holds no permission to.

show.event: two bordered service cards struck through, then the live scopes line

beats.narration_text: There is one route that runs the other way, and it is configured. Deep linking. An instructor picks a piece of content from inside Canvas, our tool hands back a pointer to it, and Canvas stores that pointer in the course. That is the only tool-to-platform message we carry.

show.event: single right-to-left arrow carrying CONTENT POINTER, everything else in mute

beats.narration_text: Which leaves a gap worth naming out loud. We built quizzes. Grading runs on our server, the client never sends a score. But with no grade service, a score has nowhere to go. It sits in our database and never reaches the Canvas gradebook. The code is honest about it: there is a comment marking the exact place where a background job would push it, and that job does not exist yet.

show.event: pipeline to a hard stop: NO ROUTE TO THE GRADEBOOK

beats.narration_text: So the research question was never how synchronisation works. It is whether we want it. Turning on grade passback means asking for a permission we removed deliberately, and reopening the data conversation we just finished having. It is a decision about scope, not a missing function.

show.event: two facing option cards, neither marked correct

beats.narration_text: So here is the honest description, as of today. One token, per click, one direction. One content pointer going back. Nothing else crosses.

show.event: three mono rows snap in, hard cut to the title restated
